ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A (very small) ball is kicked off from point A on a square billiard table with side length $2 \mathrm{~m}$. After moving along the shown path and touching the sides three times as indicated, the path ends in point $B$. How long is the path that the bal travels from A to B? (As indicated on the right: incident angle = emergent angle.)

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a square tabletop, with the side length given in the problem as 2 m. Point A is marked at the lower-left corner of the square, and point B is marked at the lower-right corner. The path shown by the arrows starts from A, first hits the right boundary, then hits the upper boundary, then hits the left boundary, and finally reaches B. The small schematic below the figure explains that during reflection, the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection. Reasoning: Use the unfolding/reflection method to handle the billiard reflection path. Because the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, each time it hits a side, reflect and unfold the subsequent square tabletop about that side, and the original broken-line path becomes a straight line. Let the side length of the original square be 2 m, with A at the lower-left corner of the original figure. The path hits the right side, the upper side, and the physical left side in order, so unfold the squares to the right, upward, and then according to the position corresponding to the physical left side. The image of the unfolded endpoint B differs from A by 6 m in the horizontal direction and 4 m in the vertical direction. So the actual broken-line path length equals the length of this straight line: sqrt(6^2+4^2)=sqrt(52)=2sqrt(13).

method.method_draft: Use the standard unfolding/reflection method. From the image, read that A is the lower-left corner and B is the lower-right corner of a square table, and the directed path hits the right side, then the top side, then the left side before ending at B. Reflect/unfold the table successively across these three encountered sides so the broken billiard path becomes one straight segment. In the unfolded grid of 2-by-2 squares, after the right, top, and physical-left reflections, the final image of B lies 6 m horizontally and 4 m vertically from A. method.method_draft: Use direct coordinate geometry with equal slopes. From the image, place the square as coordinates A=(0,0), B=(2,0), with the path A -> right side -> top side -> left side -> B. Let the absolute slope of every segment be s, because equal-angle reflection preserves the angle with each wall, changing only the sign of the appropriate component. The first segment from A to the right side has horizontal run 2, so its height is 2s. The second segment reaches the top y=2, so its horizontal run is (2-2s)/s and the top-hit x-coordinate is 2-(2-2s)/s=4-2/s. The third segment runs to the left side, giving left-hit height 2-s(4-2/s)=4-4s. The last segment from the left side to B has horizontal run 2 and vertical drop 2s, so the left-hit height is also 2s. method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中是一个正方形台面，左下角标为 A，右下角标为 B。折线路径从 A 出发，先碰到右边界，再碰到上边界，再碰到左边界，最后到达 B；下方小示意图说明反射时入射角等于出射角。

推理：设正方形坐标为 0≤x≤2, 0≤y≤2，令 A=(0,0), B=(2,0)。由于每次反射满足入射角等于出射角，所以各段路径与水平边或竖直边所成角对应保持一致，可令每一段的斜率绝对值为 s。

第一段从 A 到右边 x=2，水平位移为 2，所以碰到右边时高度为 2s。

第二段从右边反射后到达上边 y=2，需要上升 2-2s，因此水平位移为 (2-2s)/s。所以上边碰撞点的横坐标为 2-(2-2s)/s=4-2/s。

第三段从上边到左边 x=0，下降量为 s(4-2/s)，所以左边碰撞点高度为 2-s(4-2/s)=4-4s。

最后一段从左边到 B=(2,0)，水平位移为 2，竖直下降为 2s，因此左边碰撞点高度也应为 2s。于是 4-4s=2s，得到 s=2/3。

各段长度分别为：第一段 sqrt(2^2+(4/3)^2)=2sqrt(13)/3；第二段 sqrt(1^2+(2/3)^2)=sqrt(13)/3；第三段同为 sqrt(13)/3；第四段同第一段为 2sqrt(13)/3。总长度为 2sqrt(13)/3+sqrt(13)/3+sqrt(13)/3+2sqrt(13)/3=2sqrt(13)。
